items.question: Q6 (Markov): is the v0 delay a context-correlation effect? {1,3}:0.8 alone ('1,3:0.8') vs with the pairwise term ('1:1.0;1,3:0.8'), subset {x[t-1], x[t-3], xhat}; R = median onset with / alone, chain and iid training contexts.
items.definition_used: R = median onset (with {1}:1.0) / median onset (alone), per train context; 95 % percentile bootstrap CI, 2000 resamples, seed 20261112, seeds resampled independently within each arm (the same resamples for every definition; R_chain/R_iid from the four arms' resamples). Onsets: registered = first activation event of the subset (events.py: step = first of the two confirming active checkpoints, q <= 0.01 and RI >= 0.001); amended C = first not-left-censored (re)activation whose Fourier coefficient at the event's checkpoint has the final sign (alternatives: first activation only; sign at both confirming checkpoints); amended E (decides at 25 %) = first single checkpoint where f * sign(pop) >= level * pop, pop = E_uniform[tanh(h) prod_A s] from the couplings by enumerating 64 windows (1,3:0.8 on {1,3}: 0.6640; 1:1.0;1,3:0.8 on {1,3}: 0.3747; 1,2,3:1.0 on {1,2,3}: 0.7616; 1:1.0;1,2,3:1.0 on {1,2,3}: 0.4820); levels 10/25/50 %; alternatives: two consecutive checkpoints (the events' persistence), log-step interpolated crossing (sub-grid, descriptive), |f|. Censored runs would count as 30,000. Branch rule (as registered): R_iid CI includes 1 (closed interval) and R_chain CI lower bound > 1 -> branch 1 (the delay came from correlated contexts; verdict 'supported' for the context-correlation explanation); R_iid CI lower bound > 1 -> branch 2 (lower-order structure delays higher order even with iid contexts; verdict 'not_supported'); anything else 'inconclusive'. Most plausible alternative reading of the CI condition: a sub-grid onset (interpolated crossing) so that ties on the 60-point grid do not put mass exactly at R = 1.

items.interpretation: Registered branch 2 under the deciding definition: with independent (iid) training contexts the pairwise term still delays the three-way {1,3} term, R_iid = 1.48 [1.38, 1.93] at E25 (registered 2.97 [1.92, 3.39]; E10 1.92 [1.39, 2.65]; E50 1.47 [1.38, 1.58]); the largest share of bootstrap resamples with R_iid <= 1 under any of the five main definitions is 0. So the v0 delay is not only a context-correlation effect: lower-order structure delays the higher-order term even with independent contexts. The chain correlation adds to it: R_chain = 2.66 [2.18, 2.85] at E25 (5.5 [3.62, 6.53] registered), R_chain/R_iid = 1.8 [1.29, 2.06] at E25 (R_chain/R_iid = 1.85 [1.23, 2.85] registered); on a log scale the iid factor is 40% of the chain factor at E25 (64% registered). Amendment E's effect-size correction matters: normalising the threshold by the population coefficient moves R_chain from 5.5 to 2.66 and R_iid from 2.97 to 1.48 (registered -> E25), but does not remove the iid delay. Amendment C changes no onset here (0 of 86 runs differ), so the amended C result equals the registered one.
items.caveats: Onsets are on the 60-point grid (ratios 1.11-1.3 between checkpoints at 20-15,623 steps), so a factor 1.5 is about two to three checkpoints; the interpolated E25 crossing gives R_iid 1.5 [1.3, 1.79], R_chain 2.55 [2.31, 2.9]. 10 seeds per arm. The E25 and E50 R_iid (1.48, 1.47) are just below the pilot preview's 1.5-3.2 (see q6_preview). E thresholds differ between the arms by design (25 % of 0.6640 = 0.1660 alone vs 25 % of 0.3747 = 0.0937 with {1}). Censored runs (no onset by 30,000 steps): 0 of 86 registered, 0 amended C, 0/0/0 at E10/E25/E50; left-censored onsets: 0 registered, 0/0/0 at E10/E25/E50.

items.interpretation: Boundary case. Under the deciding E25 onset R_iid = 1.29 [1, 1.48]: the CI includes 1 only at its lower edge, because 13.2 % of resamples put both medians on the same checkpoint (R exactly 1) and 0 % fall below 1; no iid run with the pairwise term crosses earlier than the earliest alone run (0 of 12). R_chain = 3.04 [2.49, 4.79] lies above 1. By the letter of the registered rule this is branch 1 (the delay of the {1,2,3} term comes from correlated contexts); the same holds at E10 (1.07 [1, 1.3]). The registered onset (1.47 [1.3, 1.69]), amended C (identical), E50 (1.3 [1.13, 1.3]) and the sub-grid interpolated E25 crossing (1.27 [1.15, 1.38]) put R_iid's CI above 1 (branch 2). Read together: with iid contexts the pairwise term delays the four-way term by a small factor (R_iid 1.07-1.47 across definitions), which the deciding definition cannot separate from 1 on this grid; most of the delay comes from the chain contexts: R_chain/R_iid = 2.35 [1.91, 4.01] at E25, R_chain/R_iid = 12.8 [8.66, 17.6] registered, R_chain/R_iid = 12.8 [11.9, 13.7] at E50.
items.caveats: (1) In chain runs with the pairwise term the {1,2,3} coefficient lingers near the 25 % level (0.121): a median of 9466.5 steps pass between its 25 % and 50 % crossings (alone chain 252, with iid 132), its values in between span 0.0893-0.24, and it dips back below 25 % after first crossing in 11 of 12 runs, so R_chain is level-sensitive (E10 1.48 [1.23, 1.69], E25 3.04 [2.49, 4.79], E25 two consecutive 6.27 [2.86, 8.06], E50 16.6 [15.5, 17.6]). (2) In those runs the registered RI onset comes after the E25 crossing in 12 of 12 runs (median 5.5 checkpoints later; RI at the crossing < min_effect in 12 of 12): chain-induced lower-order coefficients (median f{2} = -0.162, f{3} = 0.175 with f{1} = 0.767) cancel the top-order log-linear term (see q6_ri_vs_fourier), which inflates the registered R_chain (18.9). (3) The iid alone arm has 10 seeds, the other three 12 (boundary refinement). Censored runs (no onset by 30,000 steps): 0 of 86 registered, 0 amended C, 0/0/0 at E10/E25/E50; left-censored onsets: 0 registered, 0/0/0 at E10/E25/E50.

items.literal_result: c13: R_iid > 1 (point) 5 of 5, CI above 1 5 of 5, R_iid in 1.5-3.2 3 of 5, R_chain > R_iid 5 of 5, R_chain in 2.9-6.1 4 of 5. c123: R_iid > 1 (point) 5 of 5, CI above 1 3 of 5, R_iid in 1.5-3.2 0 of 5, R_chain > R_iid 5 of 5, R_chain in 2.9-6.1 1 of 5. Amendment B: '1,2,3:1.0' registered onsets chain [162, 273] (12 of 12 within 162-273), iid [96, 125] (10 of 10 within 96-125).
items.interpretation: For the v0 comparison ({1,3}:0.8) the preview's direction is confirmed: R_iid > 1 with the CI above 1 in 5 of 5 definitions and R_chain > R_iid in 5 of 5. Magnitudes: R_iid 1.47-2.97 (outside 1.5-3.2: E25, E50), R_chain 2.66-5.5 (outside 2.9-6.1: E25); the deciding E25 values sit just below the previewed ranges. For {1,2,3}:1.0 R_iid is smaller than previewed (point estimates 1.07-1.47, in 1.5-3.2: 0 of 5) and its CI lies above 1 only for registered, amended_C, E50, while R_chain > R_iid in 5 of 5. The Amendment B preview of the alone {1,2,3}:1.0 onsets is reproduced exactly (12 of 12 chain, 10 of 10 iid within the previewed ranges).
items.caveats: The preview did not name the comparison or the levels it used; agreement is judged on both comparisons and all five main definitions.

items.question: Sanity checks behind Q6: subset presence, event table vs recomputed events, sign conventions, population coefficients, left-censoring and censoring, Amendment C's effect on these onsets.
items.definition_used: Planted subset looked up by name in every curve and required to be a ground-truth entry; events recomputed with detect_events(curve, alpha=0.01) and compared with ri_events (kind, step, step_lo); planted sign = sign of the population coefficient (Markov code 1 = spin +1, beta > 0, so +); final sign = sign of f at step 30,000; population coefficients by exact 64-window enumeration, checked against closed forms.

items.interpretation: The inputs behave as designed: every curve holds the planted subset, the event table matches a recomputation, no onset is left-censored or censored, and the final Fourier coefficients carry the planted (+) sign and reach about their population values. Amendment C's correction (initial wrong-sign or left-censored detections) does not apply to these order-3 and order-4 subsets, so C equals the registered onset in every run. The required population values are reproduced (0.6640, 0.3747; closed forms tanh(0.8) and (tanh(1.8) - tanh(0.2))/2).
items.caveats: The event 'step' is the first of the two consecutive active checkpoints (the onset, in (step_lo, step]); the state machine confirms it one checkpoint later (reg_confirm_step in per_run). E crossings use the same convention (first checkpoint at or above the level).

items.question: Descriptive: why does the registered RI onset diverge from the Fourier (E) onset, most strongly for {1,2,3} with the pairwise term in chain contexts?
items.definition_used: Per run, the checkpoint gap registered onset - E25 crossing; the stored RI, the single-mode RI of f(A), and an RI rebuilt from the stored Walsh coefficients f(B) of every nonempty B in A (uniform probes: E[2p-1 | x_A] = sum_B f(B) chi_B; f(empty) not stored, set to 0), all at the E25 crossing; the lower-order coefficients there.

items.interpretation: In every other arm the RI activation precedes the E25 crossing, by 2 to 13 checkpoints (RI's detection threshold corresponds to a lower coefficient). In chain runs of '1:1.0;1,2,3:1.0' it follows it (12 of 12 runs, median 5.5 checkpoints later): at the crossing f{1,2,3} is 0.122-0.143, whose single-mode RI would be 0.00799 nats (median), but the stored RI is 0.000103 (median; below min_effect in 12 of 12). The RI rebuilt from all stored coefficients (median 0.000275; within 0.002 nats of the stored value in 11 of 12) reproduces the near-zero value from the chain-induced lower-order coefficients (medians f{2} = -0.162, f{3} = 0.175 next to f{1} = 0.767), which cancel the top-order log-linear term. So this is the instrument measuring a different (log-domain) quantity, not a bug, and it is why the registered R_chain for {1,2,3} (18.9) is far above the E25 value (3.04). RI onset after the E25 crossing in the other arms: c13|alone|chain 0 of 10, c13|alone|iid 0 of 10, c13|with|chain 0 of 10, c13|with|iid 0 of 10, c123|alone|chain 0 of 12, c123|alone|iid 0 of 10, c123|with|iid 0 of 12.
items.caveats: The rebuild is approximate (f(empty) unknown, the probe's x_A marginal only nearly uniform) and sensitive near cancellation: in chain runs with the pairwise term its difference from the stored plug-in RI at the E25 crossing ranges -0.000393 to 0.00562 nats; its largest error over all checkpoints is 0.0252 nats, reached where the stored RI is already large (median 0.0509 nats there).

items.question: Descriptive: the v0 delay R (DR0, chain contexts) next to v1's chain result.
items.definition_used: DR0 ri_events, first activation of {x[t-1], x[t-3], xhat} in the 7 '1,3:0.8' and 7 '1:1.0;1,3:0.8' control-markov runs (v0: chain contexts only, 15,000 steps, 30 checkpoints); same bootstrap as v1.
items.interpretation: v1's chain runs reproduce the v0 delay (R_v0 5.12 [2.67, 9.5] vs v1 chain 5.5 [3.62, 6.53]). With independent contexts the registered R is 2.97, and 1.48 with the effect-size-normalised E25 onset (chain: 2.66): part of the v0 delay was the context correlation, part the smaller target coefficient, and a factor of 1.48 remains with iid contexts (q6).
items.caveats: v0 differs in budget (15k steps), grid (30 points) and seeds (7); a qualitative cross-check only.
